diveTitle: What actually happens when you convert
diveSubtitle: The details that matter once you go beyond the basics.
dive1Title: What happens to PNG transparency in the PDF
dive1Desc: PDF pages don't support transparency the way PNG does — any transparent areas in your PNG are filled with white in the resulting PDF page. If your image relies on a transparent background, expect it to appear as solid white once converted.
dive2Title: What order will my images appear in?
dive2Desc: Images convert into PDF pages in the exact order you arrange them before converting — drag any thumbnail to reorder it. The order in the preview grid is exactly the page order of the final PDF.
dive3Title: Screenshots vs. photos saved as PNG
dive3Desc: PNG is common for both screenshots — sharp edges, flat colors, text — and photos saved losslessly. Both convert identically into PDF pages, though screenshots typically produce smaller PDF pages since they compress more efficiently even losslessly.
dive4Desc: Each uploaded PNG becomes its own page in the PDF — there's no option to place multiple images on one page in this tool. For a layout with several images per page, you'd need a different document layout tool.
dive5Title: How big will the resulting PDF be?
dive5Desc: Roughly the sum of your PNG file sizes plus a small amount for the PDF's page structure. PNGs are often larger than equivalent JPGs to begin with, so a PDF from PNG source images tends to be bigger than one built from JPGs of the same photos.
dive6Title: Mixing PNG with JPG or HEIC
dive6Desc: This tool is built for PNG input. If you have a mix of PNG and JPG images to combine into one PDF, check whether your batch upload accepts both — most of our converters do, so check the upload screen before assuming you need to convert formats first.
faqSubtitle: Here's what people ask us most about PNG to PDF conversion.
faq1Question: Is this PNG to PDF converter really free?
faq1Answer: Yes, free to start. No hidden costs, no watermarks on your PDF, and no hassle. Just upload your images and download your PDF.
faq2Question: What image formats can I convert to PDF?
faq2Answer: We support PNG, JPG (JPEG), and WEBP. If you have images in other formats like BMP or TIFF, you'll need to convert them first — though PNG and JPG cover the vast majority of use cases.
faq3Question: Will my images lose quality when converted to PDF?
faq3Answer: No. We preserve the original quality of every image. There's no re-compression or quality loss during the PDF creation process. Your images will look exactly the same inside the PDF as they do as standalone files.
faq4Question: Can I control the page size and orientation?
faq4Answer: Absolutely. Before converting, you can choose between A4, Letter, and Legal page sizes, or use the 'Fit to Image' option that sizes each page to match the image dimensions exactly. You can also set the orientation to portrait, landscape, or let the tool decide automatically.
faq5Question: How many images can I combine into one PDF?
faq5Answer: On the free plan you can combine up to 5 images in a single conversion — Starter unlocks 10 at once, Pro unlocks 20. Each image becomes one page in the PDF, in whatever order you arrange them. Need to merge more? Convert in batches and then merge the resulting PDFs using our Merge PDF tool.
seoTitle: Why Convert PNG Images to PDF?
seoPara1: PDF is the universal format for sharing documents. It looks the same on every device, can't be accidentally edited, and is accepted everywhere — from email attachments to professional submissions. When you have a collection of PNG or JPG images that need to travel together, converting them to a single PDF is almost always the right move. It keeps everything organized, reduces the number of files you need to manage, and makes sharing a one-click action.
seoPara2: Our converter is built for people who care about the end result. We preserve the full resolution of your images and let you control exactly how they're laid out in the document. Whether you want each image to fill an A4 page, fit a Letter-size layout, or simply match its natural dimensions, the choice is yours. And because the whole process runs in your browser, there's nothing to download and no subscription to sign up for.
seoSubtitle: Common Ways People Use This Tool
seoPara3: Students scan handwritten notes and combine them into a single PDF for submission. Photographers compile proofs for client review. Designers package mockups into a clean presentation deck. Small business owners assemble receipts and invoices into a single PDF for accounting. Real estate agents combine property photos into a shareable document.
